translation_notes: The canonical sparql_literal case: a static, unparametrised query text with its own PREFIX block, assigned to a module constant and passed whole to g.query(). The module constant QUDT_QUERY9 disappears -- its text becomes the s{ } island directly at the g.query() call site, and the four PREFIX lines (BASF_EC_RaMPO, owl, rdfs, rdf) move out of the query text into @prefix declarations at module scope, inherited into the island's prologue (querying.md). Single island in the function, so the call suffix s{ ... }(g) was used rather than a @graph declaration (same threshold as the acquirium remove/_apply_graph_write precedent: a declaration would cost a line to save a parenthesis).

The query text itself -- two UNION branches, two owl:unionOf/rdf:rest*/rdf:first property paths, an OPTIONAL, five FILTERs -- is copied verbatim into the island with no rewriting: s{ } is all of SPARQL, so nothing here needed simplifying to fit. Its only syntactic risk is the ambiguity between a SPARQL group and an {expr} interpolation, and since none of this query's { ... } blocks are also valid Python expressions, none of them are misread; transpiling this file is itself the demonstrated proof (rdfeval check transpiles before it runs the driver).

Finding worth flagging: rdflib's g.query(TEXT) evaluates the query EAGERLY, so in the original the printed 'query init time' is where the real cost is measured and 'query exec time' after the for-loop is ~0. s{ } is a lazy prepared query (querying.md: 'the island's value is a lazy prepared query'): the translated program measures ~0 for init and the real cost for exec instead -- same total work, different attribution between the two printed numbers. Confirmed empirically (see driver.py's manual run): original prints init=0.028/exec=0.000, translated prints init=0.000/exec=0.028 on the same fixture. Not a defect -- s{ }'s laziness is documented and intended -- but a program that timed only the 'init' half, or asserted on it, would silently start measuring the wrong half of the work after translation. This is exactly the kind of print-only side effect run_pair's entry/calls path does not capture from stdout (see design record 405): the driver instruments a Probe stand-in for the graph to record the actual consumed ?item values instead, which is what proves the two versions agree on results despite disagreeing on where the printed timings land.
The graph parameter g arrives as a plain, unannotated positional argument (no missing-binding problem here -- unlike the self.graph cases the 163/1196 note in AGENT_BATCH warns about).

Repair 2026-10-30: the s{ ... }(g) translation described in the notes above was wrong and is withdrawn. The repository calls run_query a second time with a kglab.KnowledgeGraph (scripts/oxrdf.py:55-57), whose query(sparql, *, bindings=None) takes no initBindings (kglab/query/mixin.py:45-71); s{ ... }(g) always calls g.query(prepared, initBindings=...), so the translation raised TypeError where the original prints its items (driver calls 22-23). Neither @graph g nor g.query(s{ ... }) helps: the island's value is not accepted by rdflib's Graph.query (AttributeError: 'PreparedQuery' object has no attribute 'algebra'). Nothing in the language queries a graph-like object whose query() lacks initBindings, so translated.ldpy keeps the original g.query(QUDT_QUERY9). Minimal case: `def run_query(g): for row in g.query(TEXT): ...` called with `kglab.KnowledgeGraph`. An s{ } runtime that omitted initBindings when it is empty would make the region expressible.

optimization_notes: Both sides: the two `duration` intermediates are inlined into their f-strings, two blank lines removed. Nothing else to compress.

optimized.ldpy is identical to optimized.py: the query text QUDT_QUERY9 is a header constant, kept byte for byte, so the region has no literal text for s{ } to take; s{ } would also move the measured cost from the 'init' print to the 'exec' print (lazy query).

Observation for the translation, not acted on here: with ../ldpy at 5b807db, `s{ … }(kg)` and `kg.query(s{ … })` both run on a minimal stand-in with kglab's `query(sparql, *, bindings=None)` signature, where the translation notes report a TypeError.
